title: Effectiveness at the net as a predictor of final match outcome in professional padel players
author: Courel-Ibáñez J, Sánchez-Alcaraz Martínez BJ, Cañas J
publisher: International Journal of Performance Analysis in Sport 15(2):632-640
notes: Opened. Observational match analysis of professional padel. More than 80% (80-83%) of points are won at the net zone. Roughly 6 out of 10 rallies finish with players at the net. Controlling the net is the single strongest predictor of winning a padel match; winning pairs score ~34% more points at the net and commit significantly fewer unforced errors from the net than losing pairs.

title: Analysis of attacking actions in professional men's padel (Análisis de las acciones de ataque en el pádel masculino profesional)
author: Sánchez-Alcaraz BJ, Courel-Ibáñez J, Muñoz D, Infantes-Córdoba P, Sáenz de Zumarán F, Sánchez-Pay A
notes: Opened. Observational analysis of 2,054 attacking shots from World Padel Tour finals. Attacking shot distribution: volleys ~65%, bandejas ~23%, smashes ~12%. Winning pairs executed 327 attacking actions vs 186 for losers; winners performed >=1 attacking action in 85% of points, whereas losers performed zero attacking actions in 47% of points. Over 64% of points featuring attacking shots finish in fewer than 3 attacking strokes.

title: Análisis del uso y eficacia del globo para recuperar la red en función del contexto de juego en pádel (Analysis of the use and efficacy of the lob to recover the net in padel)
author: Muñoz Marín D, Courel-Ibáñez J, Sánchez-Alcaraz Martínez BJ, Díaz García J, Grijota Pérez FJ, Muñoz Jiménez J
notes: Opened. Analyzed 416 positional exchange actions transitioning from defense to offense. Players show a significant tactical preference for the lob over groundstrokes/passing shots (60.6% vs 39.4%) when recovering the net from the baseline, which substantially increases the likelihood of keeping the point alive and seizing offensive court position.

title: Exploring game dynamics in padel: Implications for assessment and training
author: Courel-Ibáñez J, Sánchez-Alcaraz Martínez BJ, Muñoz D
publisher: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research 33(7):1971-1977
notes: Opened. Decision-tree analysis of tactical match dynamics. Baseline defensive play relies heavily on corner glass rebounds and high lobs to neutralize opponent net pressure. The lob breaks the offensive rhythm of opponents and resets territorial control.

title: Stroke Analysis in Padel According to Match Outcome and Game Side on Court
author: Ramón-Llin J, Guzmán JF, Martínez-Gallego R, Muñoz D, Sánchez-Pay A, Sánchez-Alcaraz BJ
publisher: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health 17(21):7838
notes: Opened. Analyzed 8,441 strokes across 1,055 points in elite padel. Winning pairs execute a significantly higher percentage of direct winners, cross-court smashes, and offensive volleys from the net zone. Groundstrokes from the back court account for higher unforced error rates when forced.

title: Comparison of service tactic formation on players' movements and point outcome between national and beginner level padel
author: Ramón-Llin J, Guzmán J, Martínez-Gallego R, Vučković G, Muñoz D, Sánchez-Alcaraz BJ
notes: Opened. Evaluates player tracking and transition speeds. Elite pairs transition to net aggressively upon serving and maintain paired positioning (tandem coverage). Beginners hesitate or stay stuck in no-man's land between the baseline and service line, conceding net dominance.

title: Ball type and court surface: A study to determinate the ball rebound kinematics on the padel wall
author: Gea-García GM, Conesa-Garre CM, Courel-Ibáñez J, Menayo Antúnez R
publisher: International Journal of Performance Analysis in Sport 21(5):704-716
notes: Opened. High-speed kinematic analysis of padel ball rebounds off glass vs concrete. Glass walls produce significantly higher acceleration, velocity retention (coefficient of restitution ~0.65-0.70), and longer bounce distance. Hard flat shots into the glass rebound fast and long into the middle of the court, handing defenders an easy setup.

title: Analysis of Game Performance Indicators during 2019 World Padel Tour
author: Escudero-Tena A, Sánchez-Alcaraz BJ, García-Rubio J, Ibáñez SJ
publisher: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health 18(9):4904
notes: Opened. Examined match-play indicators across professional tournaments. Net dominance and error minimization are the highest predictors of winning sets. Players who remain on the baseline convert far fewer points and surrender offensive initiative.

title: Performance in padel
author: Escudero-Tena A, Antona D, Muñoz D
notes: Opened. Narrative review of physiological and tactical demands in padel. Points average 10-15 seconds, 8-10 shots per point in pros; active play is 30-35% of match time. Emphasizes error avoidance: more points end in unforced/forced errors than clean winners; aggressive flat hitting carries disproportionate error penalty.

title: Match Analysis, Physical Training, Risk of Injury and Rehabilitation in Padel: Overview of the Literature
author: Demeco A, de Sire A, Marotta N, Spanò R, Lippi L, Palumbo A, Iona T, Gramigna V, Palermi S, Leigheb M, Invernizzi M, Ammendolia A
publisher: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health 19(8):4159
notes: Opened. Systematic overview of padel biomechanics and injury risks. Lateral epicondylitis (padel elbow) is the most frequent upper-limb condition, driven by repetitive microtrauma to extensor carpi radialis brevis (ECRB). High impact shock and vibration from solid composite rackets without strings, combined with large wrist-snapping tennis strokes and off-center hits, drastically elevate tendon strain.

title: Incidence, prevalence and nature of injuries in padel: a systematic review
author: Dahmen J, Emanuel KS, Fontanellas-Fes A, Verhagen E, Kerkhoffs GMMJ, Pluim BM
notes: Opened. Systematic review of 8 studies (2,022 players). Injury incidence: ~3 per 1,000 h of training and 8 per 1,000 match hours. Elbow is the #1 upper-limb injury site, followed by shoulder (rotator cuff/impingement) and knee/ankle. Tendinous and muscular injuries predominate.

title: Prevention of padel injuries
author: Bernal B
notes: Opened. Over 20% of padel injuries involve lateral epicondyle tendinopathy. Shoulder rotator cuff injuries occur frequently from overhead smash decelerations. Recommends equipment customization (round racket shape, soft foam core, correct grip size to reduce forearm grip strain) and eccentric strengthening of forearm extensors and scapular stabilization.

title: Analysis of differences in injuries in padel players according to sport-specific factors, level of physical activity, adherence to the Mediterranean diet, and psychological status
author: Rocamora-López G, Mateo-Orcajada A
notes: Opened. Observational study of 216 club padel players. 54.2% reported an injury; tendons account for 30.6% and muscle 43.6%. Shoulder (14.8%) and elbow (10.5%) are primary upper-limb sites. Heavy rackets (365-375+ g) and head-heavy balances strongly associate with tendon strain.

title: Rules of Padel
author: International Padel Federation (FIP)
notes: Opened. Official court specifications: 10 m wide x 20 m long. Net height 0.88 m center, 0.92 m ends. Rear glass wall 3 m + 1 m mesh. Racket specifications: max 45.5 cm length, 26 cm width, 38 mm thickness; solid perforated surface without strings; compulsory wrist cord (max 35 cm). Ball bounce specification: 135-145 cm rebound from 2.54 m.

title: Essential tips on padel overheads, bandeja & the smash / Tips to play and improve padel lobs
author: Lawn Tennis Association (LTA Padel)
notes: Opened. Technical breakdown of padel-specific overhead mechanics. Bandeja is the antidote to the lob, hit at eye/ear height with open racket face and slice, finishing across the neck ('like a scarf'). Flat smash should only be played close to the net on short lobs. Lob must bounce deep between service line and back glass. Volley requires continental grip, compact backswing (racket never behind lead shoulder), and downward slice.

title: Brain Game Tennis ATP Tour Analytics: Net points won vs baseline points in modern tennis
author: O'Shannessy C
publisher: Brain Game Tennis / Infosys ATP Tour Data
notes: Opened. Analysis of ATP Tour match charting data. In modern professional tennis, baseline play accounts for over 75-80% of all points played. Players win ~65-67% of net approaches, but only approach the net on ~15-20% of points, spending the vast majority of points entrenched at the baseline. Contrasts sharply with padel, where >80% of all points are won at the net.
